title: Cedar VPC handoff — weekly sync pre-read + actions
content:
Purpose:
Quick pre-read for the Cedar customer weekly sync. This is a working scratchpad — will prune before sharing with Cedar contacts. Use as talking points + action tracker.

Meeting details (standing cadence):
- Weekly technical sync, Thu 10:30 PT (30 min) — internal pre-brief 10:00 PT
- Attendees: Cedar infra (Anita K.), Cedar Sec (Hiro T.), Solutions Eng (Maya S.), Private Deploy eng lead (Oliver P.), Onsite AM (Diego A.)

High-level status (one-liner):
- Network & VPC peering: done (routing quirk remains)
- On-prem infra: images deployed to staging; orchestration failing on kubelet TLS rotation
- Data plane: initial perf tests green but mem spikes at 60k tokens/session
- SLA gating items: automated failover test pending

Agenda (10:30 sync):
1) Quick round (2 min each) — current pain points
2) Network follow-up (5 min) — routing rule that drops UDP health checks (owner: Rina)
3) Kubelet TLS rotation failure (8 min) — logs, repro, temporary mitigation (owner: Oliver)
4) Memory spike hypothesis & next steps (8 min) — config diff, OOM kills (owner: Maya)
5) Action review + next sync (5 min)

Notes / fresh observations (raw):
- Routing quirk: when customer runs NAT gateway + AWS Transit, UDP probes to the nodeport are dropped intermittently. Suspect iptables conntrack timeouts + kube-proxy mode conflict. Rina to reproduce with tc/netem and post pcap.
- Kubelet TLS rotation: nodes attempt to refresh certs but fail on POST /rotate because kubelet namespace role binding missing for the deployment agent. This only shows up after a config drift where the agent SA lost permission in staging cluster. Ticket logged.
- Mem spikes: observed during concurrent multi-stream sessions; heap profile shows large KV cache growth when prefix caching hits are low. Suspect long-tail requests without cache reuse cause per-session cache retention.
- Performance note: using q8_0 quantization lowered p99 CPU, but GPU memory still climbs unexpectedly when KV cache is not pruned between sessions.

Open blockers (priority):
- BLOCKER A (high): kubelet cert rotation failing — prevents staging -> prod promotion. Owner: Oliver Park. ETA: 2026-03-12 (target to test patch). Mitigation: restart KMS agent + grant temporary role binding as workaround.
- BLOCKER B (high): UDP health checks dropping — flaky failover in customer infra. Owner: Rina Cho (Cedar eng), Redwood SRE support: Diego. ETA: 2026-03-15.
- BLOCKER C (med): memory spike on long sessions — affects cost and p99 latency. Owner: Maya Singh. Investigation: reproduce with session storm harness (use perf/cedar/session-flood). ETA: 2026-03-18 for root cause.

Action items (tracked):
- [ ] Oliver: finish kubelet rotation fix branch, add unit that checks SA permissions. Linked PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ops/PR-389. (due 2026-03-12)
- [ ] Rina: share pcap + netem scenario and confirmation whether NAT + Transit replicates. Post to Slack thread. (due 2026-03-13)
- [ ] Maya: run session-flood with KV cache pruning flag toggled (-cache-prune=on) and attach heap profiles. (due 2026-03-14)
- [ ] Diego: schedule replay window with Cedar infra team for automated failover test and own runbook steps. (due 2026-03-13)
- [ ] Oliver & Solutions Eng: draft short comms for Cedar PM on rollout timeline shift (if any). Keep language minimal and options-focused. (due 2026-03-13)

Decisions to validate in meeting:
- Agree to temporary role binding workaround vs. rolling node drain for TLS rotation. Tradeoffs: security vs. speed.
- Approve extended memory diag window on production (1-hour window, low traffic) to capture long-tail sessions. Requires PM signoff.

Notes to self (do not share raw):
- Keep the wording about prod exposure conservative — Cedar legal is sensitive to "data plane instability" phrasing. Use "performance anomalies under stress" instead.
- If we suggest temporary role binding, include an expiry and audit steps.
- Check with infra on whether we can enable node-local conntrack tuning without customer schedule conflict.

Meeting prep checklist (internal, 10:00 pre-brief):
- [ ] Confirm Rina has pcap + reproducer attached to ticket CEDAR-2147.
- [ ] Pull logs for kubelet rotate errors from last 48h (helper: /ops/log-collector/run --ticket CEDAR-2147).
- [ ] Load heap profile samples into speedscope / pprof (Maya).
- [ ] Draft 2-slide summary for Cedar PM with options (Oliver).

Follow-up format after meeting (template):
- Subject: Cedar weekly sync notes — <date>
- One-line summary
- Blockers and new action owners (table)
- Next meeting: date/time
- Links: tickets, PRs, heap profiles

Potential risks & mitigation ideas:
- Risk: if we enable node-local conntrack tuning, other services on the cluster could be impacted. Mitigation: schedule maintenance window + run canary on a single AZ.
- Risk: granting temporary elevated SA can show up in auditor logs unexpectedly. Mitigation: automated expiry + manual audit steps noted in comms.

Quick reference commands (for debugging):
- Collect kubelet rotate errors: kubectl -n kube-system logs daemonset/rotate-agent --since=72h | grep rotate
- Capture conntrack stats: sudo conntrack -L --numeric > /tmp/conntrack-$(date +%s).txt
- Run session-flood harness (local): go run ./perf/session-flood --target cedar-staging --concurrency 150 --duration 10m

Next steps (my TODOs immediately after sync):
- Merge kubelet rotation PR behind feature flag and run canary on staging cluster in AZ-a.
- Draft comms to Cedar PM (options + timeline) and share with Maya & Diego for sign-off.
- Bookmark follow-up tickets and set reminders for dates above.

-- end of scratchpad (will tidy before publish)
